```{r setup}
## Plain-text signed number with a true minus sign (for ggplot labels).
txt_signed <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "",
         paste0(ifelse(round(x, digits) > 0, "+", ifelse(round(x, digits) < 0, "\u2212", "")),
                formatC(abs(round(x, digits)), format = "f", digits = digits)))
}
pp <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(round(x, d), format = "f", digits = d)
cnt <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")

LOSE_REG_45  <- sum(trc[GRADE %in% c("4", "5")]$lose_region, na.rm = TRUE)

  band <- if (rule == "AUTO") "K–12" else "Grades 3–12"
  bc[YEAR == year & RULE == rule & as.character(BAND) == band]
}

SR_CY <- state_cut(CY, "REVIEW")

hist_auto <- function(year, std) st(year, std, "pct_auto")
HIST_YEARS <- setdiff(YRS, CY)
max_pl_shift_45 <- tr[YEAR == CY & GRADE %in% c("4", "5"), range(mean_pl_shift)]

## Youden excess of grades 4–5 over the other ILEARN grades.
if (nrow(ily)) {
  ily[, GRADE := as.character(GRADE)]
  Y_OTHER <- median(ily[!GRADE %in% c("4", "5")]$best_cut_median)

} else { Y_OTHER <- NA_real_; Y_45 <- c(NA_real_, NA_real_) }
```

## Roadmap {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Roadmap for the talk
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em;"}
1. **What changed** &mdash; a new scale in 2025&ndash;26, new proficiency levels in 2026&ndash;27
2. **Why grades 4 and 5** &mdash; the exit cut on WIDA's vertical scale
3. **2026 exit impact** &mdash; old versus new standards, by grade
4. **Is it stable?** &mdash; the new standards applied to 2024 and 2025
5. **Policy options** &mdash; keep 5.0, grade-specific cuts, or grade bands
6. **Summary of results** &mdash; and questions for IDOE
:::

::: {.key-insight}
The comparison is exact: the same **`r cnt(N_CY)`** 2026 composite scores are classified under the current and the new proficiency-level tables. Statewide, auto-exit moves from **`r pp(AUTO_OLD)`%** to **`r pp(AUTO_NEW)`%**. By grade, it moves a great deal.
:::

::: {.notes}
Headline up front: neutral statewide, redistributive by grade. The rest of the deck explains why grades 4 and 5 move down, why grade 1 and the upper grades move up, and what Indiana could do about it.
:::


# What changed {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section one: what changed
:::


## Two changes, one year apart

```{r timeline}
#| output: asis
emit_html('
<div class="timeline">
  <div class="step"><span class="when">Through 2024&ndash;25</span>
    ACCESS 2.0 composite scale. Grade-specific cut scores define proficiency levels 1.0&ndash;6.0. Indiana exits on the <b>Overall composite PL</b>.</div>
  <div class="step"><span class="when">2025&ndash;26</span>
    WIDA introduces a <b>new vertical composite scale</b> (100&ndash;600, not comparable to the old one). Scores are reported with the <b>old</b> PLs, carried over by concordance.</div>
  <div class="step new"><span class="when">2026&ndash;27</span>
    WIDA standard setting yields <b>new PLs</b> on the new scale. The October 2026 concordance gives both PL tables for every new-scale score, grades K&ndash;12.</div>
  <div class="step policy"><span class="when">Indiana policy</span>
    Exit rules are written in PL numbers: <b>5.0 auto-exit</b> (K&ndash;12) and <b>4.3&ndash;4.9 review</b> (grades 3+). The numbers stay the same; the scores behind them move.</div>
</div>')
```

::: {.key-insight}
Nothing about a student's 2025&ndash;26 performance changes. What changes is **which scale score earns a 5.0 or a 4.3** &mdash; and that change is not the same size, or even the same direction, in every grade.
:::

::: {.notes}
Two separate events. The scale changed last year, but because WIDA concorded the old proficiency levels onto the new scale, every reported PL in 2025-26 meant exactly what it meant before. Standard setting is the first time the PLs themselves change. Indiana's rule is written in PLs, so standard setting is what moves exit eligibility.
:::


## Indiana's exit rule and what this analysis does

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Current IDOE rule (Overall composite PL)**

- **5.0 or higher** &rarr; exits EL status, any grade K&ndash;12
- **4.3&ndash;4.9, grades 3+** &rarr; review-eligible; the ILP committee decides
- Below 4.3, or below 5.0 in K&ndash;2 &rarr; remains EL

In this deck, **auto-exit** means PL 5.0+, and the **exit region** means auto-exit plus review-eligible.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**The comparison**

- Take each student's 2026 new-scale composite score.
- Look up the PL under the **current** table (what was reported) and under the **new** 2026&ndash;27 table.
- Apply the same Indiana rule to both.

Same students, same scores, two PL tables. The only thing that differs is the standard.
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Assumptions to confirm with IDOE: the Overall composite is the only exit criterion (no domain minimums), and 2026 performance stands in for what 2026-27 performance will look like.
:::


## Data and method {.smaller}

```{r data-method}
#| output: asis
nrow_y <- vapply(YRS, function(y) {
  v <- vs[YEAR == y]
  note <- if (y == CY) "New scale; both PLs are exact concordance lookups" else
    "Old scale; converted to the new scale with WIDA&rsquo;s production transform"
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td style="text-align:left">%s</td></tr>',
          y, cnt(v$n), paste0(pp(v$pct_pl_match), "%"), paste0(pp(v$pct_exit_match, 2), "%"), note)
}, character(1))
within01 <- min(vs[YEAR != CY]$pct_pl_within01)
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.72em">
  <thead><tr><th>Year</th><th>Valid ACCESS records</th><th>Reported PL reproduced</th><th>Exit status reproduced</th><th style="text-align:left">How the new PL is obtained</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Reproduction: the current-standard PL looked up from the concordance, compared with the PL on Indiana&rsquo;s file. In 2024 and 2025, %s%% or more of reported PLs are reproduced to within 0.1.</div>',
paste(nrow_y, collapse = ""), pp(within01, 2))))
```

- **Concordance:** WIDA ACCESS Concordance Table, updated October 2026, Overall composite, grades K&ndash;12, every new-scale score 100&ndash;600.
- **2026:** the reported PL equals the concordance&rsquo;s current-standard PL for **every** student, so the old-versus-new comparison is exact.
- **2024 and 2025:** robustness checks. Old-scale scores are converted with `widaACCESS_2026_scale_score_transformation()` (`SGPstateData`), rounded, and looked up in the new PL table. Applied to the 2026 old-scale scores, this route reproduces the exact exit classification for **`r pp(min(mc$pct_exit_agree))`&ndash;`r pp(max(mc$pct_exit_agree))`%** of students in each grade.
- Only aggregates leave the analysis. Counts below `r SMALL_N` are suppressed.

::: {.notes}
The 2026 result is not an estimate: it is the same scores classified two ways. The history years go through WIDA's score transform and so carry a small amount of slippage at level boundaries; the method check on 2026 bounds that slippage.
:::


# Why grades 4 and 5? {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section two: the exit cut on the vertical scale
:::


## The 5.0 exit cut on the new vertical scale

```{r cut-articulation}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel line chart, one panel for the auto-exit cut (PL 5.0) and one for the review cut (PL 4.3). For each grade from K to 12 it plots the new-scale composite score at the cut under the current standards (grey) and the new standards (purple), with grades 4 and 5 shaded. On the current standards the cut falls from grade 3 to grade 4, circled where a cut is lower than the grade before; on the new standards the cut rises every grade."
cl <- rbind(
  lad[THRESHOLD == 5.0, .(GRADE, STANDARD, CUT = CUT_SS_NEW, RULE = "Auto-exit cut (PL 5.0)")],
  lad[THRESHOLD == 4.3, .(GRADE, STANDARD, CUT = CUT_SS_NEW, RULE = "Review cut (PL 4.3)")]
)
cl[, G := as.integer(GRADE)]
cl[, STD := factor(STANDARD_LABELS[STANDARD], levels = STANDARD_LABELS)]
dips <- cl[order(RULE, STD, G)][, .(G, CUT, prev = shift(CUT)), by = .(RULE, STD)][!is.na(prev) & CUT < prev]
ggplot(cl, aes(G, CUT, colour = STD)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 5.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#E6E6E1") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = dips, aes(G, CUT), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 8,
             stroke = 1.3, colour = WARN_COL, fill = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ RULE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = STD_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:12, labels = c("K", 1:12)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "New-scale composite score at the cut",
       title = "On the vertical scale, the current cuts fall from grade 3 to 4; the new cuts rise every grade",
       subtitle = "Current cuts: WIDA's concordance images of the 2024–25 cuts. Circled: lower than the grade before.") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
This is the hypothesis from the earlier New Hampshire and Indiana work, now confirmed with WIDA's own numbers. On a vertical scale the score needed to exit should not fall as grade rises. The concorded current cuts do fall at grade 4 - by 14 points at 5.0 and 13 at 4.3 - because WIDA's old grade 4-5 cuts were set relative to a different test form. Standard setting removed the dip. It also lowered the grade 1 cut, which sat almost on top of grade 2.
:::


## How far each cut moved

```{r cut-deltas}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.0
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel bar chart of how far each grade's cut moved on the new scale, in points, for the auto-exit cut (PL 5.0) and the review cut (PL 4.3), grades K to 12. Red bars above zero mark grades where the new standard is harder to reach; green bars below zero mark grades where it is easier. Grades 4 and 5 rise by 20 or more points and grade 1 falls by about 35."
dd <- pc[, .(GRADE, G = grade_factor(GRADE), DELTA,
             RULE = ifelse(THRESHOLD == 5.0, "Auto-exit cut (PL 5.0)", "Review cut (PL 4.3)"))]
ggplot(dd, aes(G, DELTA, fill = DELTA > 0)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = TEXT_COL, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = txt_signed(DELTA, 0), vjust = ifelse(DELTA > 0, -0.4, 1.3)), size = 6) +
  facet_wrap(~ RULE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = WARN_COL, `FALSE` = AUTO_COL), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.14)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "Change in cut (points)",
       title = "Grades 4–5 must now score 20+ points higher to exit; grade 1 about 35 points lower",
       subtitle = "Red: the new standard is harder to reach than the current one. Green: easier.") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
Read this as the size of the change for a student at the margin. In grades 4 and 5 the new auto-exit cut is 24 and 20 points higher. In grade 1 it is 35 points lower. In grades 7 to 12 it is 5 to 18 points lower, so those grades become somewhat easier to exit. Kindergarten, grade 2 and grade 6 barely move.
:::


## Translating the current cuts into new levels {.smaller}

```{r cut-translation}
#| output: asis
rows <- vapply(GRADES, function(gr) {
  a <- pc[THRESHOLD == 5.0 & GRADE == gr]; b <- pc[THRESHOLD == 4.3 & GRADE == gr]
  cls <- if (gr %in% c("4", "5")) ' class="hl-row"' else ""
  dcls <- function(x) if (x > 0.05) "rt-down" else if (x < -0.05) "rt-up" else ""
  sprintf('<tr%s><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%d</td><td>%d</td><td class="rt-new %s">%s</td><td>%d</td><td>%d</td><td class="rt-new %s">%s</td></tr>',
          cls, pretty_grade(gr), a$CUT_OLD, a$CUT_NEW, "", fmt_pl(a$NEW_PL_AT_OLD_CUT),
          b$CUT_OLD, b$CUT_NEW, "", if (as.integer(gr) >= REVIEW_MIN_GRADE) fmt_pl(b$NEW_PL_AT_OLD_CUT) else
            paste0('<span style="color:#9a9a96">', fmt_pl(b$NEW_PL_AT_OLD_CUT), "</span>"))
}, character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.68em;max-width:86%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead>
    <tr><th></th><th colspan="3" class="grp grp-new">Auto-exit (current PL 5.0)</th><th colspan="3" class="grp grp-new">Review floor (current PL 4.3)</th></tr>
    <tr><th>Grade</th><th>Current cut</th><th>New 5.0 cut</th><th>New PL at current cut</th><th>Current cut</th><th>New 4.3 cut</th><th>New PL at current cut</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">New-scale composite scores. &ldquo;New PL at current cut&rdquo; is the 2026&ndash;27 PL a student scoring exactly at today&rsquo;s cut would receive. Review floors for K&ndash;2 are shown in grey (no review band below grade 3).</div>',
paste(rows, collapse = ""))))
```

::: {.notes}
The right-hand columns are the bridge to the policy options. A grade 4 student who just reaches today's 5.0 would be reported as a 4.4 under the new levels; a grade 1 student who just reaches today's 5.0 would be a 6.0. Everywhere else the translation is within about half a level of 5.0.
:::


## Where students sit relative to the cut (2026)

```{r histograms}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| fig-alt: "Six histograms of 2026 new-scale composite scores in 5-point bins, as a percentage of each grade, for grades 1, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 11. A dashed grey line marks the current 5.0 cut and a solid purple line the new 5.0 cut, with the band between them shaded. In grades 4 and 5 the new cut is above the current one, so the students between the cuts lose auto-exit; in grades 1, 3, 8 and 11 it is below, so they gain it. Bins with fewer than 10 students are suppressed."
HG <- c("1", "3", "4", "5", "8", "11")
h <- hist26[GRADE %in% HG & !is.na(pct)]
h[, FACET := factor(paste("Grade", pretty_grade(GRADE)), levels = paste("Grade", pretty_grade(HG)))]
cuts <- pc[THRESHOLD == 5.0 & GRADE %in% HG]
cuts[, FACET := factor(paste("Grade", pretty_grade(GRADE)), levels = levels(h$FACET))]
ggplot(h, aes(BIN + HIST_BIN / 2, pct)) +
  geom_rect(data = cuts, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(xmin = pmin(CUT_OLD, CUT_NEW), xmax = pmax(CUT_OLD, CUT_NEW), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "#E8DDEE") +
  geom_col(width = HIST_BIN * 0.92, fill = "#9a9a96") +
  geom_vline(data = cuts, aes(xintercept = CUT_OLD), colour = OLD_COL, linetype = "22", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(data = cuts, aes(xintercept = CUT_NEW), colour = NEW_COL, linewidth = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ FACET, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(250, 550, 50)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(230, 540)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "2026 new-scale composite score (5-point bins)", y = "% of grade",
       title = "Grades 4–5 lose the students between the two cuts; grades 1, 3, 8 and 11 gain them",
       subtitle = "Dashed grey: current 5.0 cut. Solid purple: new 5.0 cut. Shaded: auto-exit status changes.\nBins with fewer than 10 students suppressed.") +
  theme_in(18)
```

::: {.notes}
How many students change status depends on two things: how far the cut moved and how many students sit in between. In grades 4 and 5 the cut moved up into the dense part of the distribution, so many students are affected. In grade 1 the cut moved down into a dense region too, so many students gain. In grade 11 the move is modest and the tail is thin.
:::


# 2026 exit impact {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section three: 2026 exit impact by grade
:::


## Statewide, almost nothing changes

```{r state-callouts}
#| output: asis
emit_html(sprintf('
<div class="callout-row">
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Auto-exit (5.0+), K&ndash;12<br>%s &rarr; %s students</div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Exit region (4.3+), grades 3&ndash;12<br>%s &rarr; %s students</div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s</div><div class="stat-label">Students whose auto-exit status changes<br>%s lose &middot; %s gain</div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Share of all auto-exits<br>that are in grades 4&ndash;5</div></div>
</div>',
pp(AUTO_OLD), pp(AUTO_NEW), cnt(NAUTO_OLD), cnt(NAUTO_NEW),
pp(REG3_OLD), pp(REG3_NEW), cnt(NREG3_OLD), cnt(NREG3_NEW),
cnt(CHANGED_AUTO), cnt(LOSE_AUTO), cnt(GAIN_AUTO),
pp(share45("OLD"), 0), pp(share45("NEW"), 0)))
```

::: {.key-insight}
The new standards are **neutral in total** &mdash; `r cnt(NAUTO_NEW - NAUTO_OLD)` more auto-exits out of `r cnt(N_CY)` students &mdash; but **`r cnt(CHANGED_AUTO)` students change auto-exit status**. Grades 4&ndash;5 lose `r cnt(LOSE_AUTO_45)`; grades 1&ndash;3 and 7&ndash;12 gain `r cnt(GAIN_AUTO)`.
:::

- Grades 4&ndash;5 are **`r pp(SHARE_N45, 0)`%** of Indiana's ACCESS takers. Today they produce `r pp(share45("OLD"), 0)`% of auto-exits; under the new standards, `r pp(share45("NEW"), 0)`% &mdash; about their share of students.

::: {.notes}
If someone only looks at the statewide rate, they will conclude nothing happened. The redistribution is the story: under the current standards more than half of all auto-exits came from grades 4 and 5; under the new standards those grades contribute roughly in proportion to their enrolment.
:::


## Auto-exit rate by grade

```{r auto-dumbbell}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell chart of the 2026 auto-exit rate, the percentage of each grade at PL 5.0 or higher, for grades K to 12 under the current standards (grey dot) and the new standards (purple dot), with each grade's change in percentage points labelled. Auto-exit in grades 4 and 5 falls by about three-quarters; in grade 1 it rises almost tenfold."
d <- rw[YEAR == CY]
d[, G := grade_factor(GRADE)]
dl <- rbind(d[, .(G, pct = pct_auto_OLD, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["OLD"]])],
            d[, .(G, pct = pct_auto_NEW, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["NEW"]])])
dl[, STD := factor(STD, levels = STANDARD_LABELS)]
ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = d, aes(x = G, xend = G, y = pct_auto_OLD, yend = pct_auto_NEW),
               colour = "#C9C9C4", linewidth = 2.4) +
  geom_point(data = dl, aes(G, pct, colour = STD), size = 6.5) +
  geom_text(data = d, aes(G, pmax(pct_auto_OLD, pct_auto_NEW) + 1.6, label = txt_signed(d_auto)),
            size = 6, colour = ifelse(d$d_auto < 0, WARN_COL, AUTO_COL)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = STD_COLS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "% of grade at PL 5.0 or higher",
       title = "Grade 4 and 5 auto-exit falls by about three-quarters; grade 1 rises almost tenfold",
       subtitle = paste0("Same ", cnt(N_CY), " students, ", CY, " scores. Labels: change in percentage points.")) +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
Grade 4 goes from 22.5 to 6.3 percent, grade 5 from 18.1 to 5.1. Grade 1 goes from under 1 percent to 6.5. Grade 3 nearly doubles, and grades 8 to 12 roughly double from a low base. After standard setting the auto-exit rate is much flatter across grades: between about 1 and 11 percent everywhere, instead of 1 to 23.
:::


## The exit region: auto-exit plus review

```{r region-bars}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| fig-alt: "Paired stacked bar chart of the 2026 exit region by grade, K to 12. Each bar stacks auto-exit (PL 5.0 and above, green) under review-eligible (PL 4.3 to 4.9, gold); the left bar of each pair, lighter and marked C, is the current standards and the right bar, marked N, the new standards. The review band applies in grades 3 and up. The exit regions in grades 4 and 5 shrink by about 20 points; those in grades 3 and 7 to 12 grow."
rr <- rw[YEAR == CY]
rl <- rbind(
  rr[, .(GRADE, STD = "OLD", COMP = "Auto-exit (5.0+)", pct = pct_auto_OLD)],
  rr[, .(GRADE, STD = "OLD", COMP = "Review-eligible (4.3–4.9)", pct = pct_review_OLD)],
  rr[, .(GRADE, STD = "NEW", COMP = "Auto-exit (5.0+)", pct = pct_auto_NEW)],
  rr[, .(GRADE, STD = "NEW", COMP = "Review-eligible (4.3–4.9)", pct = pct_review_NEW)]
)
rl[, x := as.integer(GRADE) + 1 + ifelse(STD == "OLD", -0.21, 0.21)]
rl[, COMP := factor(COMP, levels = c("Review-eligible (4.3–4.9)", "Auto-exit (5.0+)"))]
rl[, ALPHA := ifelse(STD == "OLD", "a", "b")]
tot <- rl[, .(pct = sum(pct)), by = .(GRADE, STD, x)]
ggplot(rl, aes(x, pct, fill = COMP, alpha = ALPHA)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.4, colour = NA) +
  geom_text(data = tot, inherit.aes = FALSE, aes(x, pct + 1.5, label = ifelse(STD == "OLD", "C", "N")),
            size = 5, colour = "#5c5c58") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Auto-exit (5.0+)" = AUTO_COL, "Review-eligible (4.3–4.9)" = REVIEW_COL)) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(a = 0.45, b = 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:13, labels = c("K", 1:12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "% of grade",
       title = "Grade 4–5 exit regions shrink by about 20 points; grades 3 and 7–12 grow",
       subtitle = "Left (C, lighter): current standards. Right (N): new standards. The review band applies in grades 3+ only.") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
The exit region in grade 4 falls from 54 to 30 percent of students and in grade 5 from 47 to 29. Grade 3 rises from 24 to 34 percent, which matters for ILP committee capacity: grade 3 becomes the grade with the most review-eligible students.
:::


## Where exits happen: counts by grade

```{r count-bars}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.0
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart of the number of 2026 ACCESS takers at PL 5.0 or higher in each grade, K to 12, under the current standards (grey) and the new standards (purple), with each count labelled. Under the new standards auto-exits move out of grades 4 and 5 and into other grades."
cn <- rbind(rw[YEAR == CY, .(G = grade_factor(GRADE), n = n_auto_OLD, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["OLD"]])],
            rw[YEAR == CY, .(G = grade_factor(GRADE), n = n_auto_NEW, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["NEW"]])])
cn[, STD := factor(STD, levels = STANDARD_LABELS)]
ggplot(cn, aes(G, n, fill = STD)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = cnt(n)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), vjust = -0.4, size = 5.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = STD_COLS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "Students at PL 5.0 or higher",
       title = paste0(cnt(NAUTO_OLD), " auto-exits today, ", cnt(NAUTO_NEW), " under the new standards; they move out of grades 4–5"),
       subtitle = paste0(CY, " ACCESS takers. Grade 4 and 5 cohorts are smaller than K–3, so their rates translate into fewer students.")) +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
In counts: grade 4 goes from about 1,940 auto-exits to about 540, grade 5 from about 1,360 to about 390. Grade 1 goes from about 70 to about 640, grade 3 from about 590 to about 1,150.
:::


## Who changes status

```{r transitions}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel bar chart of students whose 2026 status differs between the two standards, by grade: auto-exit (PL 5.0 and above) for grades K to 12, and the exit region (PL 4.3 and above) for grades 3 to 12. Red bars below zero count students who lose status and green bars above zero count students who gain it. Within each grade the changes run one way: grades 4 and 5 lose, grades 1 to 3 and 7 to 12 gain. Counts of 1 to 9 are suppressed."
tt <- rbind(
  trc[, .(G = grade_factor(GRADE), RULE = "Auto-exit (5.0+)", DIR = "Lose", n = -lose_auto)],
  trc[, .(G = grade_factor(GRADE), RULE = "Auto-exit (5.0+)", DIR = "Gain", n = gain_auto)],
  trc[as.integer(GRADE) >= REVIEW_MIN_GRADE, .(G = grade_factor(GRADE), RULE = "Exit region (4.3+), grades 3–12", DIR = "Lose", n = -lose_region)],
  trc[as.integer(GRADE) >= REVIEW_MIN_GRADE, .(G = grade_factor(GRADE), RULE = "Exit region (4.3+), grades 3–12", DIR = "Gain", n = gain_region)]
)
tt[is.na(n), n := 0]
ggplot(tt, aes(G, n, fill = DIR)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = TEXT_COL, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = tt[n != 0], aes(label = cnt(abs(n)), vjust = ifelse(n > 0, -0.35, 1.3)), size = 5.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ RULE, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Lose = WARN_COL, Gain = AUTO_COL)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) scales::comma(abs(x)), expand = expansion(mult = 0.12)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "Students",
       title = "Within each grade, changes run one way: grades 4–5 lose, grades 1–3 and 7–12 gain",
       subtitle = "Students whose 2026 status differs between the two standards. Counts of 1–9 suppressed (shown as 0).") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
Within any grade, everyone moves in the same direction because the whole PL table shifted one way. No student in grade 4 or 5 gains exit; no student in grades 1, 3 or 7-12 loses it. Kindergarten and grade 6 lose a handful (suppressed). In total `r cnt(LOSE_REG_45)` grade 4-5 students would leave the exit region and become ordinary EL students again.
:::


# Is it stable? {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section four: the new standards applied to 2024 and 2025
:::


## Auto-exit by grade, 2024&ndash;2026

```{r history-auto}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| fig-alt: "Three-panel line chart, one panel each for 2024, 2025 and 2026, of the percentage of each grade at PL 5.0 or higher, grades K to 12, under the current standards (grey) and the new standards (purple). 2026 is exact; 2024 and 2025 are converted with the score transform. The grade 4 and 5 peak under the current standards disappears under the new standards in every year, and grade 1 rises in every year."
hl <- rbind(rw[, .(YEAR, G = as.integer(GRADE), pct = pct_auto_OLD, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["OLD"]])],
            rw[, .(YEAR, G = as.integer(GRADE), pct = pct_auto_NEW, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["NEW"]])])
hl[, STD := factor(STD, levels = STANDARD_LABELS)]
hl[, FACET := factor(paste0(YEAR, ifelse(YEAR == CY, " (exact)", " (via score transform)")),
                     levels = paste0(YRS, ifelse(YRS == CY, " (exact)", " (via score transform)")))]
ggplot(hl, aes(G, pct, colour = STD)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ FACET) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = STD_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:12, labels = c("K", 1:12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "% at PL 5.0 or higher",
       title = "The grade 4–5 peak disappears in every year; grade 1 rises in every year",
       subtitle = "Current standards: the PL Indiana reported. New standards: each year's scores classified with the 2026–27 PL table.") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
Under the current standards grades 4 and 5 have been the exit peak every year: about 17 percent in 2024 and 2025 and higher in 2026. Under the new standards that peak is gone in every year. The grade 1 increase is larger in 2024 and 2025 (12 to 13 percent) than in 2026 (6.5 percent): 2026 first graders scored lower on the old metric than earlier cohorts did, so fewer of them sit near the new cut.
:::


## Exit region by grade, 2024&ndash;2026 (grades 3&ndash;12)

```{r history-region}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| fig-alt: "Three-panel line chart, one panel each for 2024, 2025 and 2026, of the percentage of each grade at PL 4.3 or higher (auto-exit plus review-eligible), grades 3 to 12, under the current standards (grey) and the new standards (purple). Under the current standards the exit region peaks in grades 4 and 5, at 43 to 54 percent; under the new standards it does not, with grades 4 and 5 at 24 to 30 percent."
hr <- rbind(rw[as.integer(GRADE) >= REVIEW_MIN_GRADE, .(YEAR, G = as.integer(GRADE), pct = pct_region_OLD, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["OLD"]])],
            rw[as.integer(GRADE) >= REVIEW_MIN_GRADE, .(YEAR, G = as.integer(GRADE), pct = pct_region_NEW, STD = STANDARD_LABELS[["NEW"]])])
hr[, STD := factor(STD, levels = STANDARD_LABELS)]
hr[, FACET := factor(paste0(YEAR, ifelse(YEAR == CY, " (exact)", " (via score transform)")),
                     levels = paste0(YRS, ifelse(YRS == CY, " (exact)", " (via score transform)")))]
ggplot(hr, aes(G, pct, colour = STD)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ FACET) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = STD_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 3:12) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "% at PL 4.3 or higher",
       title = "Under the new standards the exit region no longer peaks in grades 4–5",
       subtitle = "Auto-exit plus review-eligible. Current standards: 43–54% in grades 4–5; new standards: 24–30%.") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
The review region tells the same story with bigger numbers. Under the new standards grade 3 is the highest grade, then grades 4-5 and 8, then a slow decline to grade 12. That is the shape you would expect if a PL means the same thing in every grade.
:::


## Statewide totals by year

```{r history-table}
#| output: asis
rows <- vapply(YRS, function(y) {
  a <- rs[YEAR == y]; b <- rs3[YEAR == y]
  sprintf('<tr%s><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td>%s%%</td><td class="rt-new">%s%%</td><td>%s</td><td>%s%%</td><td class="rt-new">%s%%</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
          if (y == CY) ' class="hl-row"' else "", y, cnt(a[STANDARD == "OLD"]$n),
          pp(a[STANDARD == "OLD"]$pct_auto), pp(a[STANDARD == "NEW"]$pct_auto),
          txt_signed(a[STANDARD == "NEW"]$pct_auto - a[STANDARD == "OLD"]$pct_auto),
          pp(b[STANDARD == "OLD"]$pct_region), pp(b[STANDARD == "NEW"]$pct_region),
          txt_signed(b[STANDARD == "NEW"]$pct_region - b[STANDARD == "OLD"]$pct_region),
          fmt_pl(state_cut(y)$cut))
}, character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.8em">
  <thead>
    <tr><th></th><th></th><th colspan="3" class="grp grp-new">Auto-exit, K&ndash;12</th><th colspan="3" class="grp grp-new">Exit region, grades 3&ndash;12</th><th></th></tr>
    <tr><th>Year</th><th>Students</th><th>Current</th><th>New</th><th>Change (pts)</th><th>Current</th><th>New</th><th>Change (pts)</th><th>Single new cut that best matches current auto-exit</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">The last column searches new-PL cuts in steps of 0.1 for the one whose statewide auto-exit share is closest to the current-standard share.</div>',
paste(rows, collapse = ""))))
```

::: {.key-insight}
Applied to earlier years, the new standards raise statewide auto-exit by `r pp(min(sapply(HIST_YEARS, function(y) hist_auto(y, "NEW") - hist_auto(y, "OLD"))))`&ndash;`r pp(max(sapply(HIST_YEARS, function(y) hist_auto(y, "NEW") - hist_auto(y, "OLD"))))` points (`r cnt(min(hist_decomp$net))`&ndash;`r cnt(max(hist_decomp$net))` students), about the size of grade 1's gain alone (`r cnt(min(hist_decomp$g1))`&ndash;`r cnt(max(hist_decomp$g1))`). The grade pattern &mdash; grades 4&ndash;5 down by `r pp(min(drop45), 0)`&ndash;`r pp(max(drop45), 0)`%, other grades flat or up &mdash; repeats every year.
:::

::: {.notes}
2026 is close to neutral; 2024 and 2025 are slightly positive, because the grade 1 gain was larger in those cohorts. A statewide-neutral single cut sits between 5.0 and 5.1 in every year. Nothing here suggests 2026 is an unusual year for grades 3 to 12.
:::


# Policy options {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section five: policy options
:::


## Option A: keep 5.0 and 4.3 on the new levels

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r option-a}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.0
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the 2026 auto-exit percentage by grade, K to 12, under the current standards (grey) and under Option A, which keeps 5.0 and 4.3 on the new proficiency levels (purple). Option A has fewer exits in grades 4 and 5 and more in grades 1 to 3 and 7 to 12."
oa <- ob[OPTION %in% c("CURRENT", "A")]
oa[, G := as.integer(GRADE)]
oa[, LAB := ifelse(OPTION == "CURRENT", STANDARD_LABELS[["OLD"]], "Option A: 5.0 / 4.3 on new PLs")]
oa[, LAB := factor(LAB, levels = c(STANDARD_LABELS[["OLD"]], "Option A: 5.0 / 4.3 on new PLs"))]
ggplot(oa, aes(G, pct_auto, colour = LAB)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(OLD_COL, NEW_COL), levels(oa$LAB))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:12, labels = c("K", 1:12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "% auto-exit (2026)", title = "Auto-exit by grade") +
  theme_in(21)
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
- **No rule change.** The PL numbers in Indiana's rule stay; WIDA's new table supplies the scores.
- **Statewide neutral:** `r pp(AUTO_OLD)`% &rarr; `r pp(AUTO_NEW)`% auto-exit; `r pp(REG3_OLD)`% &rarr; `r pp(REG3_NEW)`% exit region in grades 3+.
- **Redistributes by grade:** fewer exits in grades 4&ndash;5, more in grades 1&ndash;3 and 7&ndash;12.
- **Consistent with the vertical scale:** a 5.0 requires a higher score in every successive grade.

::: {.key-insight}
Option A accepts WIDA's judgment that a 5.0 should mean the same thing in every grade.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
This is the default if Indiana does nothing. It inherits WIDA's standard setting directly. Its cost is concentrated: grade 4 and 5 families and teachers who expect the usual exit numbers will see far fewer.
:::


## Option B: grade-specific rate-preserving cuts

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="46%"}
```{r option-b-table}
#| output: asis
rows <- vapply(GRADES, function(gr) {
  a <- gc_cy[RULE == "AUTO" & GRADE == gr]; ap <- gc_pool[RULE == "AUTO" & GRADE == gr]
  r <- gc_cy[RULE == "REVIEW" & GRADE == gr]; rp <- gc_pool[RULE == "REVIEW" & GRADE == gr]
  cls <- if (gr %in% c("4", "5", "1")) ' class="hl-row"' else ""
  sprintf('<tr%s><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s%%</td><td class="rt-new">%s</td><td>%s</td><td class="rt-new">%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
          cls, pretty_grade(gr), pp(a$pct_old), fmt_pl(a$cut), fmt_pl(ap$cut),
          if (nrow(r)) fmt_pl(r$cut) else "&mdash;", if (nrow(rp)) fmt_pl(rp$cut) else "&mdash;")
}, character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.62em">
  <thead>
    <tr><th></th><th></th><th colspan="2" class="grp grp-new">Auto-exit cut</th><th colspan="2" class="grp grp-new">Review floor</th></tr>
    <tr><th>Grade</th><th>Current auto-exit</th><th>%s</th><th>2024&ndash;26</th><th>%s</th><th>2024&ndash;26</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">New-PL cut (steps of 0.1) whose share at or above is closest to the current-standard share.</div>',
CY, CY, paste(rows, collapse = ""))))
```
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{r option-b-chart}
#| fig-width: 9.6
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the new-scale score needed to auto-exit, by grade from K to 12, for the current 5.0 cut (dashed grey), Option A's new 5.0 cut (purple) and Option B's grade-specific rate-preserving cut (gold), with grades 4 and 5 shaded. Option B follows the current cuts and rebuilds the drop from grade 3 to grade 4 that the new 5.0 cut removes."
bcut <- merge(gc_cy[RULE == "AUTO", .(GRADE, cut)],
              lad[STANDARD == "NEW", .(GRADE, cut = THRESHOLD, SS_B = CUT_SS_NEW)], by = c("GRADE", "cut"))
bl <- rbind(
  lad[THRESHOLD == 5.0 & STANDARD == "OLD", .(G = as.integer(GRADE), SS = CUT_SS_NEW, LAB = "Current 5.0 cut")],
  lad[THRESHOLD == 5.0 & STANDARD == "NEW", .(G = as.integer(GRADE), SS = CUT_SS_NEW, LAB = "Option A: new 5.0 cut")],
  bcut[, .(G = as.integer(GRADE), SS = SS_B, LAB = "Option B: rate-preserving cut")]
)
bl[, LAB := factor(LAB, levels = c("Current 5.0 cut", "Option A: new 5.0 cut", "Option B: rate-preserving cut"))]
ggplot(bl, aes(G, SS, colour = LAB, linetype = LAB)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.5, xmax = 5.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#E6E6E1") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(OLD_COL, NEW_COL, REVIEW_COL)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("22", "solid", "solid")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:12, labels = c("K", 1:12)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1), linetype = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "Score needed to auto-exit",
       title = "Option B rebuilds the grade 4 dip") +
  theme_in(20)
```

::: {.warning-box}
::: {.warning-box-title}
Rate preservation undoes the vertical articulation
:::
Holding each grade's rate takes new-PL cuts from **`r fmt_pl(AUTO_CUT_RANGE[1])`** (grade 4) to **`r fmt_pl(AUTO_CUT_RANGE[2])`** (grade 1), putting the exit score back on the current, non-vertical path.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
These cuts are very stable across years: the 2026 and pooled 2024-26 columns differ by at most 0.1. That stability is the point: they reproduce the old cut structure, including the grade 3-to-4 drop, so they would preserve the old rates by preserving the old anomaly. A grade 4 student would exit at a lower score than a grade 3 student.
:::


## Option C: grade-band cuts

```{r option-c}
#| output: asis
bands <- c(names(GRADE_BANDS))
brow <- vapply(bands, function(b) {
  a <- bc[YEAR == CY & RULE == "AUTO" & as.character(BAND) == b]
  r <- bc[YEAR == CY & RULE == "REVIEW" & as.character(BAND) == b]
  gs <- GRADE_BANDS[[b]]
  rates <- ob[OPTION %in% c("CURRENT", "C") & GRADE %in% gs]
  detail <- paste(vapply(gs, function(gr) sprintf("%s: %s&rarr;%s", pretty_grade(gr),
      pp(rates[OPTION == "CURRENT" & GRADE == gr]$pct_auto), pp(rates[OPTION == "C" & GRADE == gr]$pct_auto)),
      character(1)), collapse = " &middot; ")
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s%%</td><td class="rt-new">%s</td><td>%s</td><td style="text-align:left;font-size:0.9em">%s</td></tr>',
          b, pp(a$pct_old), fmt_pl(a$cut), if (nrow(r)) fmt_pl(r$cut) else "&mdash;", detail)
}, character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.76em">
  <thead><tr><th>Band</th><th>Current auto-exit</th><th>Band auto-exit cut</th><th>Band review floor</th><th style="text-align:left">Auto-exit by grade under the band cut, current &rarr; Option C (%%)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">%s ACCESS takers. Band cuts are new-PL cuts (steps of 0.1) matching each band&rsquo;s current share at or above 5.0 (auto) and 4.3 (review, grades 3+).</div>',
paste(brow, collapse = ""), CY)))
```

::: {.key-insight}
Bands preserve each band's total but not its grades. In the 3&ndash;5 band, a single `r fmt_pl(bc[YEAR == CY & RULE == "AUTO" & as.character(BAND) == "3–5"]$cut)` cut **triples grade 3 auto-exit** (`r pp(g(3, "pct_auto_OLD"))`% &rarr; `r pp(ob[OPTION == "C" & GRADE == "3"]$pct_auto)`%) while still cutting grade 4 by `r pp(100 * (1 - ob[OPTION == "C" & GRADE == "4"]$pct_auto / g(4, "pct_auto_OLD")), 0)`% and grade 5 by `r pp(100 * (1 - ob[OPTION == "C" & GRADE == "5"]$pct_auto / g(5, "pct_auto_OLD")), 0)`%. Grade 3 behaves like the grades above it; grades 4&ndash;5 are the outliers.
:::

::: {.notes}
Bands are a compromise that does not fit the data well. The anomaly is specific to grades 4 and 5, and the 3-5 band straddles the break. Any band that keeps grades 4-5 near their old rates has to treat grade 3 very generously.
:::


## A single cut for all grades

```{r single-cut}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel line chart with one line per year, 2024, 2025 and 2026, of the share of students at or above a single cut on the new proficiency-level scale, for cuts from 4 to 6. The left panel is the auto-exit share for grades K to 12 and the right panel the exit-region share for grades 3 to 12. Dashed lines give each year's share under the current standards, and a purple vertical line marks Indiana's current PL number, 5.0 on the left and 4.3 on the right. The curves meet the dashed lines at about those numbers, so 5.0 and 4.3 on the new levels already match today's statewide exit shares."
sc <- rbind(
  ccs[, .(YEAR, CUT, pct = pct_new, ref = pct_auto_old, FACET = "Auto-exit share, K–12 (current: PL 5.0+)")],
  cc3[, .(YEAR, CUT, pct = pct_new, ref = pct_ge43_old, FACET = "Exit-region share, grades 3–12 (current: PL 4.3+)")]
)
refs <- unique(sc[, .(YEAR, ref, FACET)])
marks <- rbind(data.table(FACET = "Auto-exit share, K–12 (current: PL 5.0+)", x = 5.0),
               data.table(FACET = "Exit-region share, grades 3–12 (current: PL 4.3+)", x = 4.3))
ggplot(sc, aes(CUT, pct, colour = YEAR)) +
  geom_vline(data = marks, aes(xintercept = x), colour = NEW_COL, linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "solid", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(data = refs, aes(yintercept = ref, colour = YEAR), linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ FACET, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = YEAR_COLS) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 6, 0.2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Single cut on the new PL scale, all grades", y = "% of students at or above the cut",
       title = "Statewide, 5.0 and 4.3 on the new levels already match today's exit shares",
       subtitle = "Solid: share at or above each new-PL cut. Dashed: that year's share under the current standards.\nPurple line: Indiana's current PL number.") +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
The curves cross the dashed reference lines almost exactly at Indiana's existing PL numbers. In 2026, 5.0 on the new levels gives `r pp(AUTO_NEW)` percent auto-exit against `r pp(AUTO_OLD)` percent today; 4.3 gives `r pp(REG3_NEW)` against `r pp(REG3_OLD)` in grades 3 and up. In 2024 and 2025 the auto-exit match sits between 5.0 and 5.1. No other single number does better.
:::


## Options compared, 2026

```{r options-compare}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.0
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of the 2026 auto-exit percentage by grade, K to 12, under the current standards and three options: A, 5.0 and 4.3 on the new proficiency levels; B, grade-specific cuts; and C, grade-band cuts. Only Option A gives a smooth profile across grades; Option B copies today's grade 4 and 5 peak; Option C creates a new peak in grade 3."
olab <- c(CURRENT = "Current standards", A = "A: 5.0 / 4.3 on new PLs",
          B = "B: grade-specific cuts", C = "C: grade-band cuts")
oo <- copy(ob)[, LAB := factor(olab[OPTION], levels = olab)]
oo[, G := as.integer(GRADE)]
ggplot(oo, aes(G, pct_auto, colour = LAB)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c(OLD_COL, NEW_COL, REVIEW_COL, "#3498DB"), olab)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:12, labels = c("K", 1:12)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Grade", y = "% auto-exit",
       title = "Only Option A gives a smooth grade profile; B copies today's peak; C creates a new one in grade 3",
       subtitle = paste0("Statewide auto-exit: current ", pp(os[OPTION == "CURRENT"]$pct_auto), "% · A ",
                         pp(os[OPTION == "A"]$pct_auto), "% · B ", pp(os[OPTION == "B"]$pct_auto), "% · C ",
                         pp(os[OPTION == "C"]$pct_auto), "%")) +
  theme_in(19)
```

::: {.notes}
All three options are close to neutral statewide, so the choice is about the grade profile, not the total. B reproduces the current profile because it is built to. C trades the grade 4-5 peak for a grade 3 peak. A is the only option whose profile follows from the vertical scale.
:::


## Independent corroboration: ILEARN {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r ilearn-chart}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.2
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart for grades 3 to 8 of the median Youden-optimal current WIDA proficiency-level cut for predicting ILEARN ELA proficiency, 2021 to 2025, with plus-or-minus one standard deviation error bars and each median labelled. Grades 4 and 5 are red and the other grades grey; a dashed line marks the median of the other grades. The grade 4 and 5 bars stand above the others."
if (nrow(ily)) {
  iy <- merge(ily, tr[YEAR == CY, .(GRADE, mean_pl_shift)], by = "GRADE")
  iy[, G := factor(GRADE, levels = as.character(3:8))]
  ggplot(iy, aes(G, best_cut_median, fill = GRADE %in% c("4", "5"))) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = Y_OTHER, colour = OLD_COL, linetype = "22") +
    geom_col(width = 0.62) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = best_cut_median - best_cut_sd, ymax = best_cut_median + best_cut_sd),
                  width = 0.15, colour = TEXT_COL) +
    geom_text(aes(y = best_cut_median + best_cut_sd + 0.04, label = fmt_pl(best_cut_median)),
              vjust = 0, size = 6.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = WARN_COL, `FALSE` = "#9a9a96"), guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3, 5)) +
    labs(x = "Grade", y = "Best WIDA cut for ILEARN ELA proficiency",
         title = "Best-predicting cut, current PLs",
         subtitle = "Median Youden-optimal cut, 2021–2025 (±1 SD)") +
    theme_in(20)
}
```
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
- A separate Indiana analysis asked which **current** WIDA PL best separates students who are and are not proficient on **ILEARN ELA** (Youden's J, 2021&ndash;2025).
- Grades 3 and 6&ndash;8: best cut about **`r fmt_pl(Y_OTHER)`**. Grades 4 and 5: **`r fmt_pl(Y_45[1])`** and **`r fmt_pl(Y_45[2])`**.
- So under the current PLs, a grade 4&ndash;5 student needs about half a level more to show the same ILEARN readiness.
- The new standards lower grade 4&ndash;5 PLs by an average of **`r pp(-max_pl_shift_45[2])`&ndash;`r pp(-max_pl_shift_45[1])`** of a level &mdash; about the same correction.
:::

::::

::: {.key-insight}
Two independent sources &mdash; WIDA's vertical scale and Indiana's own ILEARN outcomes &mdash; point to the same conclusion: current grade 4&ndash;5 PLs run high.
:::

::: {.notes}
The ILEARN analysis is from the IN ILEARN-WIDA ACCESS sandbox (step 05, exit_grade_consistency). It was done on the old scale and old PLs, before the concordance existed, so it is a genuinely independent check. A Youden optimum is not a recommended exit number; what matters here is the relative position of grades 4-5.
:::


# Summary of results {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section six: summary of results
:::


## Do the new standards dramatically change exit rates?

::: {.answer style="font-size:1.4em; margin-bottom:0.4em"}
Not statewide. Yes, by grade.
:::

```{r summary-q1}
#| output: asis
emit_html(sprintf('
<div class="callout-row">
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Statewide auto-exit, %s</div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Grade 4 auto-exit</div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Grade 5 auto-exit</div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s%%<span class="arrow">&rarr;</span>%s%%</div><div class="stat-label">Grade 1 auto-exit</div></div>
</div>', pp(AUTO_OLD), pp(AUTO_NEW), CY, pp(g(4, "pct_auto_OLD")), pp(g(4, "pct_auto_NEW")),
pp(g(5, "pct_auto_OLD")), pp(g(5, "pct_auto_NEW")), pp(g(1, "pct_auto_OLD")), pp(g(1, "pct_auto_NEW"))))
```

- **`r cnt(CHANGED_AUTO)`** students (`r pp(100 * CHANGED_AUTO / N_CY)`%) change auto-exit status. Apart from fewer than 10 each in kindergarten and grade 6, **every student who loses auto-exit is in grade 4 or 5** (`r cnt(LOSE_AUTO_45)`).
- Grade 3 nearly doubles (`r pp(g(3, "pct_auto_OLD"))`% &rarr; `r pp(g(3, "pct_auto_NEW"))`%) and grades 8&ndash;12 roughly double from low bases.
- The pattern is the same when the new standards are applied to 2024 and 2025.
- The cause is **cut articulation**: on WIDA's vertical scale the current grade 4&ndash;5 cuts sit below grade 3's, and the current grade 1 cut sits almost at grade 2's. Standard setting removed both.

::: {.notes}
One-sentence answer: the new standards keep Indiana's statewide exit rate but move exits from grades 4 and 5 to grades 1 through 3 and the upper grades.
:::


## What cuts would preserve today's exit rates? {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{r summary-q2}
#| output: asis
rows <- vapply(GRADES, function(gr) {
  a <- gc_cy[RULE == "AUTO" & GRADE == gr]; r <- gc_cy[RULE == "REVIEW" & GRADE == gr]
  sprintf('<tr%s><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td class="rt-new">%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
          if (gr %in% c("1", "4", "5")) ' class="hl-row"' else "",
          pretty_grade(gr), fmt_pl(a$cut), if (nrow(r)) fmt_pl(r$cut) else "&mdash;")
}, character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.64em">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade</th><th>Auto-exit cut (new PL)</th><th>Review floor (new PL)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s<tr class="dim-row"><th colspan="3">Statewide single cut: %s auto-exit &middot; %s review floor (grades 3&ndash;12)</th></tr></tbody>
</table>', paste(rows, collapse = ""), fmt_pl(SC_CY$cut), fmt_pl(SR_CY$cut))))
```
:::

::: {.column width="56%"}
- **Grade by grade,** keeping each grade's rate needs auto-exit cuts from **`r fmt_pl(AUTO_CUT_RANGE[1])`** to **`r fmt_pl(AUTO_CUT_RANGE[2])`** and review floors from **`r fmt_pl(REV_CUT_RANGE[1])`** to **`r fmt_pl(REV_CUT_RANGE[2])`**. They are stable across 2024&ndash;2026 to within 0.1.
- Those cuts rebuild the current score path, **including the grade 4 drop**. They preserve rates by preserving the anomaly.
- **Statewide,** the rate-preserving single cut is **`r fmt_pl(SC_CY$cut)`** for auto-exit and **`r fmt_pl(SR_CY$cut)`** for the review floor &mdash; Indiana's current numbers. Pooled over 2024&ndash;2026 the auto-exit match is `r fmt_pl(SC_POOL$cut)`.

::: {.key-insight}
To keep today's **total**, Indiana need not change anything. To keep today's **grade profile**, Indiana would need 13 grade-specific cuts that contradict the new vertical scale.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
Be precise about the two senses of "same percentage". The statewide percentage is preserved by 5.0 and 4.3 as they stand. The grade-level percentages need grade-specific cuts, and those cuts are only "right" if the old grade 4-5 exit peak reflected real readiness.
:::


## Is a single cut for all grades tenable?

::: {.answer style="font-size:1.4em; margin-bottom:0.4em"}
Yes &mdash; and the new scale is built for one.
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**For a single cut (5.0 / 4.3)**

- The new cuts rise in every grade: a single PL now requires more English in every successive grade.
- It matches the statewide exit share in every year examined.
- ILEARN outcomes independently say current grade 4&ndash;5 PLs run about half a level high.
- It is the rule Indiana already has; nothing changes in policy text.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**What it costs**

- Grade 4&ndash;5 auto-exits fall by `r pp(min(drop45_cy), 0)`&ndash;`r pp(max(drop45_cy), 0)`% in the first year.
- Grade 1 exits rise substantially; IDOE may want to look at whether a K&ndash;1 exit at 5.0 reflects readiness.
- Grade 3 has the most review-eligible students: `r cnt(N_REV_G3_NEW)`, up from `r cnt(N_REV_G3_OLD)`.
:::

::::

::: {.key-insight}
The real policy question is not the cut but the history: **did the old grade 4&ndash;5 exit peak reflect readiness, or an articulation artifact?** The vertical scale and the ILEARN evidence both say artifact.
:::

::: {.notes}
Give the straight answer: yes. The new standards are what make a single cut defensible, because for the first time the cut scores articulate across grades. The cost is real and concentrated, which leads into the considerations slide.
:::


## Considerations for IDOE

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Communication**

- Districts with large grade 4&ndash;5 EL populations will see far fewer exits in spring 2027. Explain in advance that the change is in the standard, not in students.
- Families: `r cnt(LOSE_REG_45)` grade 4&ndash;5 students in the exit region today would not be under the new standards.

**Review-band capacity**

- Grade 3 review-eligible students rise from `r cnt(N_REV_G3_OLD)` to `r cnt(N_REV_G3_NEW)`, the most of any grade. Grade 3 ILP committees may need support.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Transition-year options**

- Adopt Option A now and monitor, or
- A one-year hold-harmless for students who met the current cut in 2025&ndash;26 (they exited under the rule in force).
- Revisit kindergarten and grade 1: the new standards make K&ndash;1 exit more common.

**Monitoring spring 2027**

- Rerun this pipeline on the first 2026&ndash;27 scores: exit rates by grade, statewide totals, and ILEARN outcomes of the new exiters.
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
These are prompts, not recommendations. The data support Option A on technical grounds; the transition choices are policy decisions for IDOE.
:::


## Discussion questions

::: {.key-insight-box}
::: {.key-insight-box-title}
Where IDOE's guidance is needed
:::
1. **Does Indiana adopt WIDA's 2026&ndash;27 levels with the current 5.0 / 4.3 rule** (Option A), knowing the grade profile of exits will change?
2. **Is the grade 4&ndash;5 drop acceptable** as a correction of an articulation artifact, or does IDOE want a transition provision for those grades?
3. **Should kindergarten and grade 1 exit at 5.0** on the new levels, given the large increase in grade 1?
4. **Is the Overall composite still the only exit criterion**, or will domain-level requirements be considered alongside the new levels?
5. **What should be monitored in spring 2027** &mdash; and reported to districts &mdash; to confirm the new standards behave as expected?
:::

::: {.notes}
Leave this up and open the floor.
:::

## Appendix: PL cut ladders on the new scale

```{r app-ladders}
#| output: asis
TH <- c(2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 4.3, 4.5, 5.0, 6.0)
cell <- function(gr, t) {
  o <- lad[GRADE == gr & STANDARD == "OLD" & THRESHOLD == t]$CUT_SS_NEW
  n <- lad[GRADE == gr & STANDARD == "NEW" & THRESHOLD == t]$CUT_SS_NEW
  ofmt <- if (is.na(o)) "&mdash;" else as.character(o)
  sprintf('<td>%s &rarr; <span class="rt-new">%s</span></td>', ofmt, if (is.na(n)) "&mdash;" else n)
}
rows <- vapply(GRADES, function(gr) sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th>%s</tr>', pretty_grade(gr),
                                            paste(vapply(TH, function(t) cell(gr, t), character(1)), collapse = "")),
               character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.66em">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade</th>%s</tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Lowest new-scale composite score at which each PL is reached: current standard &rarr; <span class="rt-new">new 2026&ndash;27 standard</span>. Source: WIDA ACCESS Concordance Table, updated October 2026, Overall. &ldquo;&mdash;&rdquo;: level not reachable on the 100&ndash;600 scale.</div>',
paste(sprintf("<th>PL %s</th>", fmt_pl(TH)), collapse = ""), paste(rows, collapse = ""))))
```

::: {.notes}
Every policy-relevant cut, both standards, all grades. The 4.3 and 5.0 columns drive the deck.
:::


## Appendix: method details {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**2026 (exact)**

- Each 2026 Overall composite score (new scale) is looked up in the concordance by grade. The current-standard PL reproduces the PL on Indiana's file for **`r pp(vs[YEAR == CY]$pct_pl_match)`%** of `r cnt(N_CY)` students.

**2024 and 2025 (robustness)**

- Old-scale scores are converted with `widaACCESS_2026_scale_score_transformation(direction = "OLD_to_NEW")` from `SGPstateData`. Where several new scores share one old score, it takes their median. Results are rounded half up.
- The new PL is looked up at the converted score. The current-standard PL is the operational PL on Indiana's file.
- Round trip (converted score &rarr; current-standard PL): `r pp(vs[YEAR == "2024"]$pct_pl_match)`% exact in 2024 and `r pp(vs[YEAR == "2025"]$pct_pl_match)`% in 2025; exit status agrees for `r pp(min(vs$pct_exit_match), 2)`%+.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Method check on 2026**

- The 2026 file also carries each student's old-scale score. Pushing those through the 2024/2025 route and comparing with the exact lookup:

```{r app-method-check}
#| output: asis
rows <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(mc)), function(i) {
  r <- mc[i]
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s%%</td><td>%s%%</td><td>%s%%</td><td>%s%%</td></tr>',
          pretty_grade(r$GRADE), pp(r$pct_pl_within), pp(r$pct_exit_agree), pp(r$pct_auto_exact), pp(r$pct_auto_hist))
}, character(1))
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.8em">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade</th><th>PL within 0.1</th><th>Exit status agrees</th><th>Auto-exit, exact</th><th>Auto-exit, via transform</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>', paste(rows, collapse = ""))))
```
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
The transform route slightly overstates auto-exit in a few grades (at most about 0.4 points), which bounds the error in the 2024-2025 robustness results.
:::


## Appendix: 2024&ndash;2026 auto-exit and exit region by grade

```{r app-history-table}
#| output: asis
hrow <- vapply(GRADES, function(gr) {
  cells <- paste(vapply(YRS, function(y) {
    r <- rw[YEAR == y & GRADE == gr]
    sprintf('<td>%s</td><td class="rt-new">%s</td>', pp(r$pct_auto_OLD), pp(r$pct_auto_NEW))
  }, character(1)), collapse = "")
  cells2 <- paste(vapply(YRS, function(y) {
    r <- rw[YEAR == y & GRADE == gr]
    if (as.integer(gr) < REVIEW_MIN_GRADE) return('<td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td>')
    sprintf('<td>%s</td><td class="rt-new">%s</td>', pp(r$pct_region_OLD), pp(r$pct_region_NEW))
  }, character(1)), collapse = "")
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th>%s%s</tr>', pretty_grade(gr), cells, cells2)
}, character(1))
yh <- paste(sprintf('<th colspan="2" class="grp grp-new">%s</th>', YRS), collapse = "")
sub <- paste(rep('<th>Cur.</th><th class="rt-new">New</th>', 2 * length(YRS)), collapse = "")
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.6em">
  <thead>
    <tr><th></th><th colspan="6" class="grp">Auto-exit (%%)</th><th colspan="6" class="grp">Exit region, grades 3+ (%%)</th></tr>
    <tr><th></th>%s%s</tr>
    <tr><th>Grade</th>%s</tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Current: the PL Indiana reported that year. New: the 2026&ndash;27 PL table applied to the same scores (2024&ndash;2025 via score transform).</div>',
yh, yh, sub, paste(hrow, collapse = ""))))
```

Full robustness table behind the "Is it stable?" section.
